title: Recent OCR work: the real AI result, the fix, and next steps
instructions: Browse at your own pace; comments are optional. Each item has its own note box. Enter your name before Save draft or Submit review. evidence.label: 1 · What has happened since the previous walkthrough
evidence.text:
We have now made one real AI request on one short passage, called S5. Qwen received the saved scan, original OCR, fixed-rule cleanup and inspection signals in one request. It returned a complete answer in 53.34 seconds, but the answer failed the software checks. No clean reading was accepted.

I then clarified the response rules and tested them without asking the model again. The latest software gate passed 1,023 tests, including 13 focused checks for this failure. That establishes software behavior, not historical accuracy.

You can comment beside every item below. This walkthrough is optional; no regrading of your earlier reviews is requested. Your earlier comments about the stray apostrophe after loyal and the damaged word property remain attached to their original cases and required future checks. They were not tested by this S5 request.

evidence.label: 4 · Why the answer could not be accepted
evidence.text:
The AI supplied just one raw-text edit:
on- Appropriations → on Appropriations

Applying that saved edit to the original OCR produces:
The Committee on Appropriations recom- mended non-concurrence.

But the returned full proposed reading also joins recom- mended to recommended. That second edit was missing from its edit list, even though fixed-rule cleanup had already suggested it. Every retained change must be listed against the original OCR, so the full sentence can be recreated exactly.

The answer also said no finding while reporting a repair, called its repair image-unclear while describing clear print, used the wrong source-anchor type, and omitted four required self-check categories. Those contradictions remain saved. I did not silently repair the old answer or turn it into an accepted result.

evidence.label: 5 · What I changed after that failure
evidence.text:
The revised instructions say exactly how to identify the original words being changed, when image evidence supports a proposed repair, and when to withhold a reading because print is unclear.

They require all nine self-check categories: all words; names and places; numbers; punctuation; printed repetition; bracketed cues; target/context boundaries; unflagged text; and existing fixed-rule edits. A completed reading must have no remaining unresolved concerns.

They also explain that every change from original OCR needs a linked edit, including a retained fixed-rule repair. Software must replay the complete edit list and recover the full proposed reading character for character. Conditional schema rules now prevent some contradictory field combinations. Other consistency checks remain enforced by the existing strict validator.

The old request still reconstructs exactly, and its saved failed answer still fails. Invented test examples cover both required edits, unchanged text, whole-paragraph concerns and honest withheld readings. No second model response exists yet. These tests do not prove that Qwen will follow the revised instructions.

evidence.label: 6 · What the timing does and does not tell us
evidence.text:
The one real request took 53.34 seconds including its cold start. The backend reported 45.08 seconds, including about 6.01 seconds loading the model. It reported 1,391 input tokens and 762 output tokens. Preparation and the first saved report brought that measured session to about 260 seconds. Total engineering effort and electricity cost were not measured.

A provisional forecast assumes 296,995 paragraphs, one paragraph per request, and the same 53.34 seconds for every request. Sending 10% of paragraphs to AI and auditing 1% of the rest would mean about 480 computer hours. Sending 25% plus the same audit rule would mean about 1,133 hours. Sending every paragraph would mean about 4,400 hours.

Those are hypothetical attempt costs, not a forecast of successful cleanup. We have zero accepted results from one attempt; useful yield, longer-passage costs, routing rates and rework are unknown. Keeping the model loaded or grouping passages might change time, but neither was measured here. The remaining six selected units are still pending; two of their images are missing. No full-collection job is proposed.

evidence.label: 7 · Optional decision: one small test of the revised instructions
evidence.text:
I recommend one additional request on this same S5 passage, using the revised instructions and response rules. Its purpose is to learn whether the model can return a useful complete repair that passes the strict checks. This passage has now been seen during development, so the result would not be an independent accuracy test.

Limits: one request to the same installed Qwen model; no retries, extra probes, downloads or source fetches; at most 1,500 output tokens and ten minutes for the whole session. Preparation gets up to 270 seconds, startup plus the request share 120 seconds, observing the owned process exit gets 30 seconds, and reporting gets 180 seconds. A missed preparation deadline means no request.

As with the first measurement, this asks to proceed before complete native input-fit evidence exists. The 6,000-input-token figure is a reporting threshold for this attempt, not a verified capacity limit. The revised literal messages measure 1,712 tokens before actual backend image/framing treatment; true fit and conditional-schema support remain unknown. The previous one-call permission is spent. New approval would apply only to this changed request and this narrow preflight exception.

After an approval, I would first pin a new one-use allowance, test the shared deadlines, freeze final code/request identities and check current processes, queue and lock. Then one request, save the raw reply and measured costs, observe the owned process stop, and report even if invalid or incomplete. An uncertain stop or ambiguous outcome blocks further calls.

You may approve, request changes, defer, or leave this unanswered and comment only. Choosing an option and submitting records your decision for the next agent turn; it does not launch a model automatically. No choice approves corpus-wide processing, rewriting original OCR, or final cleanup policy. Other offline work can continue without this decision.
